thread:
Maria Gomez: quick heads-up from this morning's smoke runs: we're seeing a consistent tail bump when the runtime picks kernel=fmha_v3 on A5000 for very short sequences (seq=8..12) and small batches (1-3).

Kevin Liu: do we have a kernel-selection trace that shows why fmha_v3 is preferred? need rule id + perf estimate to debug.

Maria Gomez: only when REDWOOD_KERNEL_DEBUG=1. sample debug output we captured in staging: 

```
[kernel_event] model=redwood-1, layer=5, seq=10, batch=2, device=RTX-A5000, chosen=fmha_v3, rule="heuristic_v4(seq<=16 && arch>=sm86 && batch>=2)", weight_format=fp16
```

Anya Patel: that freeform reason string is painful to aggregate. we should emit structured fields in telemetry: kernel_id, rule_id, perf_pred_us, perf_alt_us, perf_obs_us, seq_len, seq_bucket, batch_size, kv_state, effective_seq_layer, arch_cap, env_flags, confidence_margin_us.

Josh Carter: microbench numbers: on A5000 fmha_v3 has higher launch/setup overhead so for seq<=12 and batch<=3 matmul_tiled is ~80-150us faster. fmha_v3 only wins at higher batch sizes.

perf-bot: [info] perf-scan started: kernautotune sweep queued at 2024-10-11T09:02:00Z

Maria Gomez: flame snippet from the microbench (cropped):

```
flame: setup_cost 0.14ms
       fmha_v3   0.56ms
       matmul_tiled 0.30ms
```

Anya Patel: setup_cost looks relatively large vs compute time for tiny workloads. also current telemetry only records kv_hit boolean. we need kv_state with categories (cold|warming|hot) and per-layer effective_seq estimates so kernel-selection logic can consider shrinkage across layers.

Kevin Liu: agreed. proposed telemetry event schema additions (strings or small ints):
- kernel_id
- rule_id
- perf_pred_us
- perf_alt_us
- perf_obs_us
- seq_len
- seq_bucket (<=16,17-64,65-128)
- batch_size
- kv_state (cold|warm|hot)
- effective_seq_layer (CSV when debug on)
- arch_cap
- env_flags
- confidence_margin_us

Maria Gomez: example emitted JSON (single-line) when REDWOOD_KERNEL_DEBUG=1:

```
{"kernel_id":"fmha_v3","rule_id":"heuristic_v4","seq_len":10,"batch_size":2,"kv_state":"warm","perf_pred_us":310,"perf_alt_us":210,"perf_obs_us":420,"arch_cap":"sm86","env_flags":"REDWOOD_KERNEL_DEBUG=1"}
```

Josh Carter: can we also include a small ranked list of top-2 candidate kernels with their perf_pred_us? that helps identify near-ties where confidence margin is tiny.

Anya Patel: yes, and add decision_confidence (0-100). console can then color picks with low confidence and offer a tooltip with the alt candidate.

infra-bot: [deploy] kerndecorate v1.4 deployed to staging at 2024-10-11T09:30:12Z

Maria Gomez: current hypothesis: our heuristic threshold for fmha_v3 on A5000 is too permissive (batch>=2). i'll submit a quick change to bump that to batch>=6 for A5000 and add a config flag REDWOOD_KERNEL_PREFERENCE=latency|throughput for testing.

Kevin Liu: please also emit perf_pred_us and perf_alt_us so we can compute confidence dynamically and possibly prefer the safer pick when margin small. i'll open PR for threshold + env flag.

Josh Carter: running a quick sweep in staging: seq in [8,10,12,16] x batch in [1,2,3,4,6,8]. will attach CSV and flame traces. ETA ~2.5h.

Maria Gomez: FYI found a small sync bug on cold KV paths that added an extra cudaEventSynchronize which inflated setup_cost. patch submitted to remove unnecessary sync unless kv_state==cold. expecting improvement for small-batch cold runs.

perf-bot: [alert] perf-regression-detector: job redwood/perf/rt-smoke reported +7% delta for redwood-1 on RTX-A5000 at 2024-10-11T09:45:03Z

Anya Patel: for console UX we'll add a kernel_choice column in trace view showing predicted vs observed latency, rule_id, and a tooltip with env_flags + per-layer kernel list when present. low-confidence picks will show an amber badge.

Kevin Liu: action items recap:
1) emit structured kernel selection telemetry (Maria)
2) raise A5000 fmha_v3 threshold to batch>=6 and add REDWOOD_KERNEL_PREFERENCE (Kevin)
3) run full perf sweep and upload artifacts (Josh)
4) show kernel_choice + predicted/observed + tooltip in console (Anya)
5) keep REDWOOD_KERNEL_DEBUG off in prod by default; enable per-customer when troubleshooting (Team)

Maria Gomez: i've filed INF-4218 for the telemetry schema + INF-4219 for console changes. assigning follow-ups. tagging @Kevin for the threshold PR review.

Josh Carter: sweep finished, initial CSV uploaded: https://internal.ci/sweeps/rt/9001/results.csv (contains per-config perf_obs_us, baseline_us, kernel_id). short summary: matmul_tiled wins for seq<=12 & batch<=4 on A5000; fmha_v3 wins for batch>=6.

Kevin Liu: PR opened: github.com/redwood/kerndecorate/pull/846 (thresholds + env flag + unit tests). running perf tests now. will hold rollout until staging sweep confirms.

Maria Gomez: after the sync-fix and threshold bump, staging smoke shows regression cleared. closing the perf alert. thanks team. :tada:

Anya Patel: i'll prototype the console tooltip and share a mock in #design next week.

Maria Gomez: final note: let's make sure telemetry captures per-layer kernel_ids when DEBUG_KERNEL_LAYER=1. these mid-sequence flips were the hardest to debug in traces.

Kevin Liu: agreed. if anyone sees more mispicks, ping me directly.
